newsitem.title: USA: US Speaker Gingrich says wants lower cap gains tax.
newsitem.headline: US Speaker Gingrich says wants lower cap gains tax.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Tuesday he hoped that tax legislation currently being crafted in the House would either reduce the maximum capital gains tax rate to no higher than 20 percent or exclude 50 percent of capital gains from taxation.

The current maximum capital gains rate is 28 percent. "My hope is it's going to be no higher than 20 percent or a 50 percent exclusion -- I prefer a 50 percent exclusion -- and I hope that they're going to index it (for inflation)," he said.
The Georgia Republican was referring to proposals to allow capital gains to be measured after taking account of inflation.
"But, I don't know anything in detail, (House Ways and Means Committee Chairman) Bill Archer hasn't told me," Gingrich said to reporters.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said earlier he would also like to see a capital gains tax reduction to a maximum rate of about 20 percent.
